entities.summary:
Virius Nepotianus was a Roman statesman and Consul of the Roman Empire in 336. He is believed to have been the husband of princess Eutropia and father of the usurper Nepotianus.

As the son-in-law of Emperor Constantine I, Virius Nepotianus played a crucial role in the tumultuous succession of the Roman Empire following Constantine's death in 337. His involvement in the power struggles of the late Roman Empire has been the subject of much debate among historians.

Virius Nepotianus's legacy is complex and multifaceted. On the one hand, his association with the usurper Nepotianus has led some to view him as a mere pawn in the game of imperial politics. On the other hand, his own rise to prominence as a Consul and his connections to the imperial family demonstrate a remarkable level of social mobility and strategic acumen.

One of the most striking aspects of Virius Nepotianus's life is the enigmatic nature of his personal relationships. His marriage to princess Eutropia, who was also the daughter of Emperor Constantine I, has been the subject of much speculation among historians. The exact nature of their relationship remains unknown, adding to the mystique surrounding this enigmatic figure.

In conclusion, Virius Nepotianus was a Roman statesman whose significance extends beyond his relatively short tenure as Consul. His involvement in the power struggles of the late Roman Empire, his connections to the imperial family, and the enigmatic nature of his personal relationships all contribute to a rich and complex historical narrative.
